title: LeanDag TUI Protocol
description: JSON protocol for communication between lean-dag and lean-tui. All field names use snake_case convention. Discriminator fields: 'type' for message/command variants (following LSP conventions), 'kind' for tagged text variants (following Lean's internal TaggedText structure). Messages are newline-delimited JSON objects.

LineCharacterPosition.description: A position in a text document following the Language Server Protocol specification. Both line and character are zero-indexed. The character offset is measured in UTF-16 code units, which matters when dealing with unicode characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.

line.description: Zero-indexed line number in the document. The first line is line 0.

character.description: Zero-indexed character offset within the line, measured in UTF-16 code units. For ASCII text, this equals the column number minus one.

FullyQualifiedDocumentPosition.description: A fully-qualified position within a document, combining a file URI with a line/character position. Used when referencing locations across different files in the workspace.

uri.description: The URI of the document, typically a file:// URI pointing to a Lean source file in the workspace.

position.description: The position within the document specified by the URI.

ServerOperatingMode.description: Indicates how the lean-dag server is running. 'Library' mode uses 'lake serve' and requires the target project to have 'import LeanDag' in its source files. 'Standalone' mode uses the lean-dag binary directly and works without any imports, but may have reduced functionality.

SubexpressionDiffTag.description: Describes how a subexpression differs between the proof state before and after a tactic application. The 'was*' variants indicate changes visible in the 'before' view, while 'will*' variants indicate changes visible in the 'after' view. Used by the TUI to render diff highlighting with appropriate colors.

SubexpressionAnnotation.description: Metadata attached to a subexpression within a tagged text tree. Currently contains only diff information, but may be extended with additional subexpression metadata in the future (e.g., hover information, semantic tokens).

diff_status.description: The diff status of this subexpression, indicating whether and how it changed between proof states. Null or absent if the subexpression is unchanged.

oneOf.description: A leaf node containing plain text with no nested structure or annotations.

text.description: The raw text content to display. May contain whitespace and newlines.

oneOf.description: An internal node that concatenates multiple child elements. Used to build complex expressions from smaller parts while preserving the tree structure.

children.description: The child elements to concatenate in order. The final displayed text is the concatenation of all children's text content.

oneOf.description: A tagged node that wraps content with subexpression metadata. Used to attach diff highlighting and other annotations to specific parts of an expression.

subexpression_info.description: Metadata for this subexpression, including diff status for before/after highlighting.

tagged_content.description: The wrapped content that this tag applies to. Can be any variant, allowing for nested tags.

AnnotatedTextTree.description: A recursive tree structure for rich text with optional annotations per subexpression. Mirrors Lean's internal TaggedText type and supports diff highlighting for before/after proof state comparison.

NavigationTargetLocation.description: A navigation target for go-to-definition or go-to-type-definition commands. Contains the file URI and position where the definition or type is located.

uri.description: The URI of the file containing the definition. Typically a file:// URI pointing to a Lean source file.

position.description: The position within the file where the definition starts, typically at the beginning of the identifier.

PreresolvedNavigationTargets.description: Pre-resolved navigation locations for an expression, hypothesis, or goal. These are computed eagerly when building the proof DAG so the TUI can navigate without additional server round-trips.

definition.description: The location of the definition of this term. For a hypothesis, this points to where the hypothesis was introduced. For a goal type, this points to the type's definition.

type_definition.description: The location of the type's definition. For a term of type T, this points to where T is defined. Useful for navigating to the structure or inductive type definition.

BindingKind.description: The kind of binding in term-mode code. 'let_bind' is a let-binding, 'fun_param' is a function parameter, 'match_var' is a pattern match variable, 'for_var' is a for-loop variable.

LocalBinding.description: Information about a local binding (variable) in term-mode code. Analogous to ProofContextHypothesis but for functional programming context.

name.description: The user-visible name of the binding as it appears in the code.

type.description: The type of the binding as an annotated text tree with diff highlighting.

value.description: For let-bindings with explicit values, the bound expression. Null for function parameters or pattern match variables.

id.description: A unique internal identifier for tracking this binding across expression nodes.

binding_kind.description: The kind of binding (let, function parameter, match variable, etc.).

is_implicit.description: True if this binding is implicit (e.g., {α : Type}).

is_instance.description: True if this binding is a typeclass instance (e.g., [Monad m]).

is_removed.description: True if this binding goes out of scope. Used for diff display.

navigation_locations.description: Pre-resolved go-to-definition and go-to-type-definition locations for this binding.

DisplayStyle.description: The display style determines which TUI mode renders this DAG. 'proof' for tactic-based proof visualization, 'dataflow' for term-mode expression data flow, 'effectflow' for monadic effect flow visualization.

GraphEdge.description: A directed edge in the graph with optional label and attributes. Used to connect nodes in the unified graph representation.

target.description: Target node ID this edge points to.

label.description: Edge label (e.g., binding name for data flow, branch label for control flow, hypothesis dependency for proofs).

kind.description: Edge kind whose interpretation depends on display style.

GraphNode.description: A node in the unified graph with content, edges, and extensible metadata. Used by all display styles (proof, dataflow, effectflow).

id.description: Unique identifier for this node within the graph.

content.description: Primary content (tactic text, expression, effect operation, etc.).

kind.description: Node kind whose interpretation depends on display style.

position.description: Source position where this node's expression/tactic appears.

parent.description: Parent node ID. Null for root nodes.

GenericDag.description: Unified DAG representation that can express proof trees, data flow graphs, and effect flow graphs. The display_style field determines which TUI mode renders this DAG and how to interpret the metadata.

display_style.description: Which display mode should render this DAG.

definition_name.description: The fully qualified name of the definition being visualized.

initial_context.description: Initial hypotheses (for proof mode) or bindings (for term-mode) available at the start.

root_node_id.description: The node ID of the root node.

current_node_id.description: The node ID closest to the cursor position.

orphans.description: Node IDs that don't have a parent in the tree structure.

EditorCursorPosition.description: Information about the current cursor position in the editor. Sent from the editor to lean-dag to request proof information at that location.

uri.description: The URI of the document where the cursor is positioned. Must match a file that has been opened in the LSP session.

position.description: The cursor position within the document, used to find the enclosing proof and current tactic.

method.description: The LSP method that triggered this cursor update (e.g., 'textDocument/hover', 'textDocument/definition'). Used for debugging and may influence response behavior.

oneOf.description: Sent when the TUI client first connects to the lean-dag server. Provides information about the server's operating mode, the port this worker is using, and the file it is handling.

server_mode.description: The mode in which the server is running, affecting available features and how the client should interact.

port.description: The TCP port this worker's server is listening on. Each worker (handling one file) gets a unique port from the configured range.

file_uri.description: The file URI this worker is handling. In library mode with per-worker ports, each file gets its own worker and port.

port_range_min.description: The minimum port in the configured port range. Clients can scan this range to discover active workers.

port_range_max.description: The maximum port in the configured port range. Clients can scan this range to discover active workers.

oneOf.description: Sent when the editor cursor moves to a new position. Allows the TUI to track cursor location even when no proof DAG is available.

uri.description: The URI of the document containing the cursor.

position.description: The new cursor position in the document.

method.description: The LSP method that triggered the cursor update.

oneOf.description: Sent when an error occurs during proof DAG extraction or other server operations. The TUI should display the error message to the user.

error.description: A human-readable error message describing what went wrong. May include technical details for debugging.

oneOf.description: Unified DAG message - dispatches to appropriate TUI mode based on display_style. Can represent proof trees, data flow graphs, or effect flow graphs.

uri.description: The URI of the document containing the definition.

position.description: The cursor position that triggered this DAG extraction.

dag.description: The unified DAG representation. The display_style field determines which TUI mode renders it.

oneOf.description: Sent when the editor focuses a file (e.g., via textDocument/didOpen or tab switch). Allows the TUI to immediately follow file switches without waiting for cursor movement.

uri.description: The URI of the file that gained or lost focus.

focused.description: True if the file gained focus, false if it lost focus.

ServerToClientMessage.description: Messages sent from the lean-dag server to the lean-tui client. Each message is a single JSON object terminated by a newline.

oneOf.description: Request the editor to navigate to a specific position. Used when the user selects a navigation target in the TUI (e.g., go-to-definition on a hypothesis).

uri.description: The URI of the file to navigate to.

position.description: The position within the file to place the cursor.

oneOf.description: Explicitly request a proof DAG at a specific position. Deprecated: the server now sends proof DAGs automatically on hover events. Kept for backwards compatibility.

uri.description: The URI of the document to extract the proof from.

position.description: The position in the document to find the enclosing proof.

mode.description: The extraction mode. Currently only 'tree' is supported. Reserved for future DAG visualization modes.

oneOf.description: Sent when the TUI client is ready to receive data. The server responds with the current cursor position and DAG if available. This allows late-connecting clients to receive the current state.

ClientToServerCommand.description: Commands sent from the lean-tui client to the lean-dag server. Each command is a single JSON object terminated by a newline.

messages.description: Server-to-TUI messages, sent as newline-delimited JSON objects.

commands.description: TUI-to-server commands, sent as newline-delimited JSON objects.
